Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

Stripe’s Product Legal team is responsible for managing the legal and regulatory elements of the design, build and execution of our products and services. We work on some of the hardest technical, commercial, and regulatory problems around. In this role you will be a key advisor to Stripe’s product, engineering and partnerships teams, and will work on a diverse set of matters that straddle financial services, business, and technology.

The ideal candidate is passionate about Stripe’s mission of helping businesses grow and thrives in solving complex legal, technology and business issues in collaboration with others. We’re looking for someone who is a team player and willing to jump in on tasks of any size. Experience in financial services, and in particular, with cryptocurrency and stablecoin products, will help you be successful in this role.

· Be part of a growing team of Product Counsel who are responsible for helping Stripe deliver products that are compliant with laws and contractual commitments to our users across the globe. The focus of this role will be on the development and commercialization of cryptocurrency and stablecoin products, particularly as part of our Bridge line of business.

· Help Stripe product teams navigate the cutting edge intersection of technological innovation, e-commerce user experiences, and financial services compliance on a range of issues.

· Actively collaborate with a wide variety of Stripe teams, including product, engineering, partnerships, compliance, risk and marketing, on a range of issues related to product development and commercialization, including advising on new and emerging legal and regulatory developments impacting products, including identifying trends and potential impacts on business activities and adapting existing laws to new technologies.

· Work closely with colleagues across Stripe’s global legal team to support Stripe's regulatory structure, its customer agreements, and strategic financial partnerships.

· Help scope and build scalable and effective processes for legal review and launch of new products.

· Stay up-to-date, with the support of Stripe’s legal subject matter experts, on US and international laws and regulations pertaining to cryptocurrency, stablecoin, and traditional financial services products.

· Participate as a proactive and strategic business partner to senior managers and be a trusted advisor.

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

· 7+ years of experience as a qualified lawyer in a top law firm, in-house legal team and/or government agency, with expertise in cryptocurrency and stablecoin product development, and related laws and regulations such as the GENIUS Act.

· Someone who is familiar with counseling teams that solve issues through technology by translating complex legal requirements into clear and actionable advice that helps the business move forward.

· Someone who works collaboratively with teammates and is always looking for opportunities to share knowledge and experience.

· A qualified US lawyer.

· A passion for technology and ability to understand complex business models and product use cases quickly.

· An entrepreneurial spirit -- a self-starter who thrives in a fast paced environment, deals well with ambiguity and focuses on driving impact.

· Excellent judgment and capable of making smart decisions with imperfect information.

· Strong communication skills (both written and verbal).

· Excellent project management skills and ability to work under tight deadlines.

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Airbnb’s Legal Department is a global team that will require working with diverse international colleagues around the world. The successful candidate will be someone who is adaptable, collaborative and embodies Airbnb’s Core Values.

Candidates will be required to approach complex legal issues with a balance for local and global perspectives, while being adaptable to cultural differences and nuances. Airbnb is looking for an Associate Counsel to join our Commercial & Technology Legal team, focusing on intellectual property transactions and open source. The ideal candidate is adaptable, collaborative, practical, and business-minded, with strong judgment and a clear commitment to Airbnb’s Core Values.

In this role you’ll partner with teams across the company to support the infrastructure and products used by millions of people worldwide, helping Airbnb innovate and move quickly while safeguarding our IP, brand, and technology ecosystem. This is transactional and counseling work, not litigation or patent prosecution.

We’re looking for someone with a genuine interest in Airbnb’s mission and a demonstrated commitment to ethics, integrity, diversity, and belonging.

Airbnb’s Legal team embodies the company’s innovative, forward-thinking spirit. At the boundary of the digital and physical world, Airbnb is building trustworthy AI and technology that mediate real-stakes interactions between real people.

Where some see obstacles, we see the opportunity to find creative, practical solutions, right at the cutting edge. Our adventurous, fast-moving legal team brings together talented, collaborative, and self-motivated professionals across the globe who believe in Airbnb’s mission and in leading as a 21st-century company.

This role sits where legal and technology meet: partnering with Airbnb’s technology and data science teams to guide how we build, share, and talk about our technology, while protecting the company’s IP.

Your work will focus on three core areas: (i) strengthening open source governance and compliance for both what we use and what we release, including the evolving overlap between open source and AI; (ii) helping Airbnb’s technology teams share their work with the world while keeping risk and messaging in check; and (iii) negotiating university research and data agreements, including IP and publication rights.

In the second core area, you’ll partner with authors from concept through publication, review external content, advise on what can go public versus stay internal, and weigh in on moonlighting and side-project requests.

You’ll also advise on IP licensing and transactions more broadly, helping our teams innovate responsibly and tell Airbnb’s technology story with confidence.

· Provide pragmatic guidance on open source licensing, compliance, and contribution practices (inbound use and outbound releases), including where open source meets AI, such as model and dataset licenses.

· Work with Engineering, Security, Infrastructure, Brand, and other teams to improve open source policies and workflows.

· Advise on open source governance topics such as:

· Usage & Contributing: internal use of third-party open source, “copyleft” risks, contributing to external projects, and CLA review.

· Owning & Releasing: when and how Airbnb code may be open sourced, quality and maintenance expectations, community and code-of-conduct considerations, and project sunsetting.

· Review external facing material (e.g., academic papers and articles, conference talks and decks, developer and community programs, technology-related blog and social posts) before publication, flagging IP, confidentiality and trade secrets, claims substantiation, third-party rights and permissions, and open source-adjacent messaging.

· Negotiate research and data agreements with public and private universities, covering sponsored research, publication rights, IP ownership, and commercial-use rights.

· Draft and review IP and licensing terms in intercompany and other commercial agreements.

· Advise senior leaders on what IP to release publicly and what to keep internal, review employee outside-work requests for IP and conflict concerns, and assess IP-contamination risk.

· Build and maintain the playbooks, templates, and training that help other lawyers and business partners handle common IP and open source questions on their own.

· Provide practical legal advice on a wide range of IP matters for data science, engineering, and business teams, including licensing issues tied to product development, tooling, and infrastructure.

· Partner with Marketing, Comms, and colleagues in Legal, and liaise with international colleagues, to keep guidance consistent across brand, marketing, and technology narratives and across regions.

· At least three years as an attorney at a law firm, in government, or in-house, including meaningful work in technology transactions and advising technical teams.

· Working knowledge of copyright, trademark, and patent fundamentals and how they apply in technology and product contexts.

· Experience drafting and negotiating IP and licensing provisions across a variety of agreements.

· Grounding in open source licensing and compliance.

· Familiarity with AI licensing, particularly where it intersects with open source.

· Strong analytical and risk-framing skills, with practical cost/benefit judgment in a fast-moving environment.

· Clear written and verbal communication, including translating complex legal issues for non-lawyers.

· Able to manage multiple matters, prioritize, and drive them to resolution with high ownership.

· Sound judgment on what to handle independently and when to escalate.

· Good sense of humor, disdain for drama, and desire to get things done.

· Passion for travel and deep appreciation for the Airbnb community.

· Licensed attorney in good standing of the bar of at least one U.S. state or territory.

· Direct experience advising engineering, data science, infrastructure, or developer platform teams.

· Familiarity with common open source licenses (e.g., MIT, Apache 2.0, GPL/LGPL, AGPL) and typical compliance workflows (e.g., dependency review, notices, attribution, policy-based approvals).

· Experience negotiating sponsored research agreements and contracting with universities, public or private.

· Exposure to marketing and advertising law in external messaging, such as FTC basics, endorsements and testimonials, substantiation, and comparative claims.

· Deeper experience with AI/ML IP issues, such as training-data rights, model and dataset licensing, and output ownership.

Who Are We?

Postman is the world’s leading API platform, used by more than 45 million+ developers and 500,000 organizations, including 98% of the Fortune 500. Postman is helping developers and professionals across the globe build the API-first world by simplifying each step of the API lifecycle and streamlining collaboration—enabling users to create better APIs, faster.

The company is headquartered in San Francisco and has offices in Boston, New York, Austin, Tokyo, London, and Bangalore - where Postman was founded. Postman is privately held, with funding from Battery Ventures, BOND, Coatue, CRV, Insight Partners, and Nexus Venture Partners. Learn more at postman.com or connect with Postman on X via @getpostman.

P.S: We highly recommend reading The "API-First World" graphic novel to understand the bigger picture and our vision at Postman.

The Opportunity

Postman's international business is growing rapidly, driven by enterprise adoption, an expanding partner ecosystem, and deepening relationships with the world's largest technology organizations across EMEA, APAC, and emerging markets. As Sr Commercial Counsel, you will be Postman's first dedicated international commercial legal hire, owning the legal work that supports this growth while operating as an extension of the US-based Commercial Legal team.

Reporting to the Managing Counsel, Commercial, you will serve as the primary legal partner for Postman's commercial and partnerships teams outside the Americas.

Your manager is based in the US (New York City), and the role is designed for a high degree of autonomy during EMEA and APAC business hours, with regular touchpoints during overlapping hours to stay aligned on priorities, positions, and escalations.

You will draft, negotiate, and close enterprise and mid-market SaaS agreements, partner and channel deals, and cross-border commercial transactions, with primary focus on EMEA and shared responsibility for APAC.

You will also help shape how Postman's commercial legal function operates internationally, adapting US contracting standards, playbooks, and processes for global markets while maintaining consistency across the legal team.

This is a high-visibility role for a commercial lawyer who wants to help build an international legal function, not just maintain one.

Commercial Contracting and Partner Support

· Serve as lead counsel for Postman's international commercial transactions outside the Americas, with primary focus on EMEA and shared coverage of APAC enterprise and mid-market deal flow.

· Draft, review, and negotiate subscription agreements, order forms, and related deal documents with large global and mid-size enterprises on both Postman paper and counterparty paper.

· Manage a high-velocity deal pipeline spanning multiple regions and time zones, partnering directly with Sales, Deal Operations, and Finance to close complex deals at the pace the business requires.

· Apply and adapt Postman's established US contracting standards, templates, and playbooks to international transactions, ensuring global consistency while addressing local legal, regulatory, and commercial requirements.

· Advise on deal structuring, pricing models, and commercial risk across EMEA and APAC jurisdictions.

· Support the legal workstream for international partner, channel, and alliance agreements, including technology partnerships, reseller and distribution arrangements, marketplace terms, co-sell and referral terms, and co-marketing agreements.

· Contribute to the scaling of Postman's global partner program by building frameworks, templates, and processes that work across jurisdictions.

International and Cross-Border Legal Support

· Navigate cross-border commercial issues that arise when a US-headquartered platform sells and partners internationally, including data transfer mechanisms, local regulatory considerations, and multi-entity deal structures.

· Collaborate with the US Commercial Legal team to maintain alignment on contracting positions, escalation protocols, and legal operations processes.

· Coordinate with external counsel in EMEA and APAC jurisdictions as needed for local law advice on specific transactions or regulatory questions.

· Contribute to global Legal team initiatives, including template development, process improvements, and enablement.

· Provide practical, commercially-minded guidance that enables internal stakeholders to move quickly and make informed decisions.

· Act as a resource for business teams based outside of the Americas on day-to-day commercial legal questions, building trust as an accessible and responsive legal partner.

· Qualified solicitor or barrister in England and Wales (or equivalent UK legal qualification) in good standing.

· Law degree (LLB, JD, or equivalent).

· 7-10 years of legal experience, including substantial in-house experience at a technology company, with significant time spent on B2B enterprise and mid-market SaaS commercial transactions.

· Direct experience drafting and negotiating partner, channel, and alliance agreements, with a working understanding of technology partnership program structures, including reseller models, marketplace distribution, referral arrangements, and OEM licensing.

· Experience working on cross-border commercial transactions within a US-headquartered company's legal framework, including familiarity with US-style contracting conventions, escalation norms, and playbook-driven processes.

· Ability to work independently across EMEA and APAC time zones while maintaining close alignment with a US-based legal team on contracting standards, positions, and priorities.

· Ability to manage a high volume of concurrent transactions with speed and sound judgment, balancing risk with commercial momentum across multiple regions.

· Strong commercial instinct and the ability to translate business objectives into contract language that protects Postman while enabling deals to close.

· Clear, confident communicator who builds strong relationships with business stakeholders across time zones and functions.

· Familiarity with US commercial contracting conventions and legal frameworks (formal US bar admission a plus but not required)

· Prior in-house experience at a high-growth SaaS, developer tools, or API-focused technology company.

· Experience supporting cloud marketplace transactions or technology partnerships.

· Familiarity with APAC and EMEA data protection requirements as they apply to commercial and partner agreements, including international data transfer mechanisms.

· Experience building or localizing contract templates, playbooks, or legal operations processes for new regions.

· Working knowledge of commercial legal requirements across multiple EMEA and APAC jurisdictions beyond the UK.

Protect Democracy is seeking an experienced, highly motivated attorney to join our team as Senior Counsel, focusing on the legal dimensions of artificial intelligence and advanced technology as they intersect with American democracy.

This role is integral to our scaling of the AI for Democracy Action Lab — Protect Democracy ’s multidisciplinary, nonpartisan “action tank” focusing on building tech tools and shaping law and policy to safeguard and strengthen democracy in the AI era.

This position is remote based in the US.* Please note: We are no longer hiring early-mid career Tech Counsel.

This is a position for candidates with at least 10 years of experience as an attorney, ideally including expertise in AI and emerging technology law, exceptional legal and analytical skills, entrepreneurial legal instincts, and a demonstrated ability to translate complex technical and legal questions for diverse audiences.

In this role, you will develop and advance legal strategies at the frontier of AI law and policy. From idea generation to execution, you will work with a small team driving creative impact litigation and other projects that integrate legal, regulatory, and communications strategies to constrain deployments of AI that are corrosive to our democracy.

You will also help build the AI for Democracy Action Lab’s expertise and credibility on the legal questions that will define how AI shapes our democracy. As a member of this team, you will shape the AI for Democracy Action Lab’s legal advocacy priorities, building upon the team’s strategies to date.

Our legal work has included advocacy to push back against the Pentagon’s retaliation against Anthropic for standing by its red lines, litigation challenging the administration’s attempt to chill online trust and safety work, and litigation and advocacy to stop the administration’s unlawful collection and aggregation of Americans’ personal data and deployment of technology for surveillance purposes.

At Protect Democracy , we believe that diversity isn’t just a strength — it’s a necessity for tackling the complex challenges facing democracy. A broad range of backgrounds, perspectives, and lived experiences strengthen our ability to analyze problems, craft solutions, and drive meaningful change.

We strongly encourage candidates from diverse backgrounds and from across the political and ideological spectrum to apply. If you meet most but not all of the criteria listed below but believe nonetheless you’d be a stellar match for the role and could grow into it, we want to hear from you.

In this role, you will: Identify, scope, and manage complex, high-stakes integrated advocacy projects to advance the AI for Democracy Action Lab’s goals; Lead and drive the development of innovative legal arguments and potential litigation approaches at the intersection of AI and democracy; Lead the process of researching, drafting, and editing pleadings, motions, briefs, and other legal filings in impact litigation; Lead communication with opposing counsel and manage and grow relationships with clients, coalition partners, experts, and government stakeholders in high-stakes litigation and non-litigation settings; Manage discovery processes, including informal fact-finding, document review, witness interviews, written discovery, depositions, and expert discovery; Supervise and mentor paralegals, junior legal staff, and law students; Write, publish, and present to key audiences on legal issues that gain significant traction at the intersection of AI and democratic governance; Brief reporters and provide expert commentary on complex legal questions and developments in AI law and regulation, serving as a public face for projects; Engage with policymakers, regulators, civil society partners, and the tech industry as a credible legal voice for pro-democracy AI governance.

Provides direct support to Army organizations to ensure program and policy compliance of the Army's Ethics Program.

KSA's: Skill in identifying and researching highly technical and complex legal issues. Skill in providing legal, technical, and policy guidance. Ability to effectively, professionally, and ethically manage a heavy caseload of clients with complex legal needs.

Qualification Requirements: The following minimum qualification requirements must be met before applicants are eligible for further consideration: Education Requirements: Position requires the possession of the first professional law degree (LL.B. or J.D.) AND active membership in the bar of the highest court of a State, U.S. commonwealth, U.S. territory, or the District of Columbia.

Applicants for initial appointment into attorney positions within the Department of Army must be graduates of law schools accredited by the American Bar Association at the time of the applicant's graduation. As indicated below, a law school transcript must be submitted with your application materials.

As noted below, proof of such membership and good standing must be submitted with your application materials.
